title: Pecorino di Fossa con Miele
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A distinctive sheep's milk cheese aged in underground pits, its intense, earthy flavor balanced simply with a drizzle of local honey and perhaps a few walnuts.
longDesc: Pecorino di fossa gets its name and character from a genuinely unusual aging method — the cheese wheels are wrapped and buried in straw-lined pits for months, a practice with roots tracing back to medieval times when hiding food stores from raiders was a practical necessity.
ingredients: 300 g (10.5 oz) Pecorino di Fossa, at room temperature
steps: Bring the cheese to room temperature before serving to allow its full flavor and aroma to develop.
Slice or crumble the pecorino onto a serving platter.
chefTips: Let the cheese sit out for at least 20–30 minutes before serving — its aroma and flavor are much duller straight from the refrigerator.
A stronger honey, like chestnut, stands up well to the cheese's intense, earthy character.
This makes an excellent simple end to a meal, in the way many Italians close dinner with cheese rather than a sweet dessert.
commonMistakes: Serving the cheese too cold, which mutes its distinctive flavor.
Pairing it with a very mild, delicate honey that gets lost against the cheese's intensity.
Cutting it too far ahead of serving, letting it dry out at the edges.
servedWith: A glass of Vin Santo or a robust red wine
storage: Store the wrapped cheese refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: A good source of calcium and protein; honey provides natural sweetness with some antioxidant compounds.
culturalNote: Pecorino di Fossa is a protected specialty of the Marche and neighboring Emilia-Romagna, its pit-aging tradition tracing back centuries to when hiding cheese from raiders and tax collectors was a genuine necessity.
